title: Magnetic cancellation narrows a stable corotation band and reduces its flux in an aligned dipole plus octupole model
abstract: We test whether a higher-order magnetic field removes stable sites near corotation in a fixed-field model for complex periodic variables. Pure aligned odd multipoles retain stable equatorial sites at corotation. For a parallel aligned dipole plus octupole, we derive the connected stable band as their known magnetic null crosses corotation. With a=3(B3/B1)/(4x squared)=1+epsilon, the band width tends to (3/4)|epsilon| times the corotation radius. The unsigned magnetic flux through this band tends to (9/16)epsilon squared in dipole flux units. We derive the global zero-stiffness boundaries and check the results with 86 field-line tests, positive flux quadrature and 100 Cartesian direction tests. The result separates local stability from the amount of flux in a stable band. It gives a specific surface-field relation to test, rather than a general loss of traps with higher multipole order. No magnetic map or new stellar data are used. Other stable sites remain; field tilt, mass loading, closure and material survival can change the result. This study does not explain a measured CPV rate or identify the cause of the hot-star deficit.

display.caption: Stable equatorial sites and unsigned magnetic flux in the connected band through corotation. The quadratic limit applies close to cancellation in an aligned fixed field. Other stable sites can remain.
